name: Miguel A. Gonzalez Almonte

bullets: Manage make-ready operations for 2,444 units across six phases, each operated as its own property.
Lead a 7-person make-ready organization (2 assistant managers, 1 coordinator, 4 technicians) and a network of outside vendors.

Run turns end to end: scheduling, vendor coordination, inspections, and readiness reporting to leasing and management, working to a seven-business-day turn standard.
Managed a $1M+ operating budget and $5M+ in capital projects across a 535+ unit operation.
Led a 7-person team (4 technicians, 2 make-ready staff, 1 housekeeper) and coordinated outside vendors.
Took an over-budget maintenance operation to roughly $30K under budget in a single month, close to 40% of the monthly budget.
Built Python reporting and KPI dashboards that replaced manual reports; audit pass rates improved about 30%. Trained 8 to 10 staff on the new tools.
Built Excel/VBA automation that cut reporting time by roughly 70% through a redesigned data model and automated aggregation.
Led scheduling, budgeting and milestone tracking for high-volume residential renovations across concurrent projects.

product.title: Make-Ready Intelligence Platform (DMRB)
product.heading: Product Case Study
product.intro: AI operations platform for apartment unit turns, proven in a live 2,444-unit residential operation: 15 daily users across 5 roles, 8+ months in production.
bullets: Found the problem from 10+ years inside operations: unit-readiness knowledge was scattered across spreadsheets, verbal updates and property-system exports, with no audit trail and no gate against premature move-ins.
Designed a 57-table PostgreSQL data model around the unit lifecycle, with append-only event history, field-level import audit trails and scoped vendor access by token.

Turned operational judgment into a deterministic rules engine: 11 breach signals (move-in risk, SLA breach, inspection breach, stale units) evaluated in strict priority order and feeding 22 ranked action queues. It flags move-in risk up to 3 business days early.
Deployed a GPT-4o assistant grounded in live data through one snapshot pipeline that the UI, the operations views and the AI all read. The AI recommends and never writes to business state.
Built anti-hallucination guardrails: intent classification, role-scoped context, server-computed summaries, token budgets, rate limiting, and a deterministic fallback when the model is unavailable.

Drove adoption across leasing, management, field and vendor users through hands-on training. The platform became the daily system of record for scheduling, vendor dispatch and SLA tracking, and supported a seven-business-day turn standard.

Scale: four production services, 950 commits across backend and frontend, 358 test files. Now leading a multi-tenant Python/FastAPI rewrite with tenant isolation, Alembic migrations and 594 tests wired into CI.

systems.title: MG-OPS, graph-first engineering knowledge system
systems.text: One SQLite graph as the single source of truth for project knowledge, with one validated write path so AI tools and scripts can't record contradictory facts. 25 entity types, 31 relationship types, 12 migrations, 1,173 graph tests.

systems.title: mg-agent, governed AI agent platform
systems.text: Typed capabilities, approval gates, 8 engine adapters, and a replay harness that tests the platform with the model held constant, including rejection of false claims of completion. 666 passing tests in the November 2026 run.

He owned the AWS infrastructure.
